## Discovery & Translational Science

- **Circulating RNA biomarker Tu-Stroma identified for early-stage ovarian cancer detection** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04755-2) — *Nature Medicine*
  - Evaluated in a 506-individual cohort, the long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) Tu-Stroma—a biomarker reflecting tumor microenvironment fitness—discriminated early-stage ovarian cancer and premalignant lesions from benign lesions.
  - Tu-Stroma demonstrated superior diagnostic sensitivity and specificity compared to standard serum CA125 testing.

- **Vascular inflammation identified as resistance driver to vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04741-8) — *Nature Medicine*
  - **[Big Pharma]** Longitudinal patient-reported outcome trajectories in ulcerative colitis patients treated with Takeda's integrin blocker vedolizumab defined underlying disease endotypes.
  - Molecular profiling implicated persistent vascular mucosal inflammation as a potential mechanism driving treatment resistance.

- **Safimaltib demonstrates potent MALT1 inhibition in B-cell lymphoma models** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43002421/) — *PubMed*
  - Preclinical characterization confirmed safimaltib as a highly selective MALT1 inhibitor with robust antiproliferative activity across preclinical B-cell lymphoma models.

- **AI multi-agent platform GPCRAgent introduced for GPCR drug discovery** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43003299/) — *PubMed*
  - Researchers introduced GPCRAgent, an open platform combining domain-specific knowledge graphs with large language models to automate target identification and lead optimization for G protein-coupled receptors.

- **Dendritic cell senescence via KDM4B-PTX3 axis predicts biologic non-response in severe asthma** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43003302/) — *PubMed*
  - Investigation of severe asthma pathology revealed KDM4B-PTX3-driven senescence in dendritic cells as a primary mediator of disease severity and a predictive marker for non-responsiveness to biologic therapies.

- **Obituary: Natural product chemist Jon Clardy (1943–2026)** [In the Pipeline](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/jon-clardy-1943-2026) — *In the Pipeline*
  - Renowned chemical biologist Jon Clardy passed away from acute myeloid leukemia.
  - Over a multi-decade career at Iowa State and Cornell, Clardy solved foundational X-ray crystal structures of complex natural products including bryostatin, saxitoxin, and brevetoxin B.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **PepGen reports positive early clinical data for PGN-EDODM1 in myotonic dystrophy type 1** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/muscular-dystrophy-dm1-pepgen-pgn-edodm1-early-results/) — *STAT*
  - Topline early-stage trial data showed PGN-EDODM1 corrected toxic CTG repeat expansions ("genetic stutters") in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1).
  - PepGen confirmed a cash balance of $105 million, providing operational funding into 2028.

- **[Biotech]** **Fate Therapeutics presents Phase 1 FT819 data in lupus at ACR 2026** [X / Twitter (@BioStocks)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120128357899891154) — *X / Twitter (@BioStocks)*
  - Phase 1 data for FT819, an off-the-shelf, iPSC-derived CD19 CAR-T cell candidate, demonstrated meaningful clinical responses in patients with severe systemic lupus erythematosus.
  - Responses were achieved without requiring standard lymphodepleting conditioning chemotherapy.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Resistance exercise mitigates lean mass loss during tirzepatide treatment** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04752-5) — *Nature Medicine*
  - A randomized trial in patients receiving Eli Lilly's dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide evaluated the impact of structured resistance training on body composition.
  - Concurrent resistance exercise significantly attenuated lean tissue loss compared to tirzepatide administration alone.

- **CD19 CAR-T cell therapy mivocabtagene autoleucel evaluated in Stiff Person Syndrome** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43002394/) — *PubMed*
  - Results from an open-label, nonrandomized clinical trial demonstrated early therapeutic activity and feasibility of mivocabtagene autoleucel (CD19 CAR-T) in patients with Stiff Person Syndrome.

- **ANGPTL4 inhibition lowers elevated triglyceride levels in clinical study** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2612463) — *NEJM*
  - Trial evaluation of an ANGPTL4-inhibiting agent demonstrated significant reductions in plasma triglyceride levels in adult patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia.

- **[Biotech]** **Beam Therapeutics reports positive Phase 1/2 BEACON data for risto-cel in sickle cell disease** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120125328056267113) — *X/BioStocks*
  - Beam Therapeutics announced positive topline results from the Phase 1/2 BEACON trial evaluating risto-cel in patients with sickle cell disease.
  - The study met its primary efficacy endpoint of freedom from severe vaso-occlusive crises for at least 12 consecutive months based on independent adjudication, alongside all primary safety endpoints.

- **[Biotech]** **PepGen reports positive Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 trial results** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120124736554606962) — *X/BioStocks*
  - PepGen released Phase 2 data from the FREEDOM2-DM1 trial evaluating a 10 mg/kg dose in myotonic dystrophy type 1.
  - The 10 mg/kg dose achieved the highest reported level of splicing correction in this setting and demonstrated improvements across multiple functional outcome measures.

- **[Biotech]** **Ovid Therapeutics advances OV329 into Phase 2 focal epilepsy study** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120126018791084274) — *X/BioStocks*
  - Ovid Therapeutics is advancing OV329 into a global Phase 2 study for focal epilepsy, with trial readout expected in H2 2027, while enrollment continues in an ongoing photosensitivity study.
  - The company reported $161 million in cash and cash equivalents.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Big Pharma]** **Divarasib shows superior PFS over first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors in Phase 3 trial** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41591-026-00057-9) — *Nature Medicine*
  - Phase 3 trial results demonstrated that Roche/Genentech's next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor divarasib significantly prolonged progression-free survival (PFS) compared to Amgen's sotorasib and BMS's adagrasib in patients with KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

- **[Biotech]** **Vir Biotechnology's HDV combo hits primary endpoints in pivotal Phase 3 study** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/vir-chronic-hepatitis-d-drug-results-elebsiran-tobevibart/874089/) — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Vir's combination regimen of elebsiran (siRNA) and tobevibart (monoclonal antibody) met all primary efficacy endpoints in a Phase 3 study for chronic hepatitis D (HDV).
  - The combination demonstrated higher viral suppression potency than competing late-stage HDV programs.

- **[Biotech]** **Azetukalner reduces focal seizure frequency in Phase 3 X-TOLE2 trial** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43002431/) — *PubMed*
  - **[Biotech]** Xenon Pharmaceuticals' selective Kv7 potassium channel opener azetukalner met its primary endpoint in the randomized Phase 3 X-TOLE2 trial in adults with drug-resistant focal seizures.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves Bayer's Sunharbo (asundexian), first-in-class Factor XIa inhibitor for stroke prevention** [FDA Press Release](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-factor-xla-inhibitor-help-prevent-stroke-certain-adults-high-risk) — *FDA Press Release*
  - FDA approved Bayer's Sunharbo (asundexian 50 mg tablets) in combination with antiplatelet therapy for secondary stroke prevention in adults following recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA).
  - Sunharbo represents the first approved Factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor, designed to reduce thrombosis risk without compounding bleeding risks associated with traditional anticoagulants.

- **FDA adds warning for rare optic neuropathy risk to GLP-1 receptor agonists** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/biotech-news-glp-1-given-an-fda-warning-for-rare-eye-condition-risk/) — *STAT*
  - FDA updated prescribing information across the GLP-1 receptor agonist class to include warnings regarding potential risks of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a condition leading to sudden vision loss.

- **FDA issues warning letters to international active pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturers** [FDA Warning Letters](http://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/nanjing-hanxin-pharmaceutical-technology-co-ltd-734913-11032026) — *FDA Warning Letters*
  - FDA CDER issued cGMP warning letters to Nanjing Hanxin Pharmaceutical Technology, Tianjin Healthcare Medical Technology, Chongqing Qiancan Technology, and USV Private Limited following critical record-review and facility inspection deficiencies.

- **FDA releases draft guidance for early-phase solid tumor IND protocols** [FDA Guidance Document](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/early-phase-ind-protocol-recommendations-solid-tumors-draft-guidance-industry) — *FDA Guidance Document*
  - FDA Oncology Center of Excellence published draft guidance containing protocol design recommendations for sponsors submitting early-phase investigational new drug (IND) applications in solid tumors.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **BioNTech acquires FDA Priority Review Voucher from Scholar Rock for $205 million** [X / Twitter (@BioStocks)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120127794730684907) — *X / Twitter (@BioStocks)*
  - BioNTech agreed to acquire a Priority Review Voucher (PRV) from **[Biotech]** Scholar Rock for $205 million in cash to expedite a future regulatory submission.

- **[Biotech]** **Ionis stock drops over $1 billion after slashing Tryngolza launch projections** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/09/ionis-pharmaceuticals-shares-plummet-after-tryngolza-slow-rollout/) — *STAT*
  - Ionis Pharmaceuticals lost over $1 billion in market valuation after significantly reducing sales expectations for Tryngolza (olezarsen), its antisense drug for severe hypertriglyceridemia, citing a slow commercial launch.

- **[Biotech]** **Oyster launches with $60 million Series A for tau-targeted protein degraders** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/oyster-venture-financing-tau-targeted-protein-degraders/874160/) — *BioPharma Dive*
  - London-based Oyster closed a $60 million Series A financing to advance targeted protein degraders designed to clear toxic tau accumulation in Alzheimer's disease.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Dutch antitrust regulator probes Biogen over MS drug and diagnostic bundling** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/10/dutch-antitrust-regulators-probe-biogen-over-multiple-sclerosis-drug-test/) — *STAT*
  - Dutch Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM) launched an investigation into Biogen regarding potential abuse of market dominance involving its multiple sclerosis drugs and associated diagnostic blood tests.

- **Trump administration removes WuXi AppTec from DoD military list** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/09/trump-administration-removes-wuxi-apptec-from-its-chinese-military-list/) — *STAT*
  - U.S. officials removed contract manufacturer WuXi AppTec from the Department of Defense designated list of Chinese military-linked companies operating in the U.S.

- **[Biotech]** **Autolus Therapeutics reports $41.2 million Q3 Aucatzyl revenue** [X / Twitter (@BioStocks)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120126685836444009) — *X / Twitter (@BioStocks)*
  - Autolus reported Q3 net product revenue of $41.2 million for its CD19 CAR-T therapy Aucatzyl, ending the quarter with $248 million in cash resources.

- **[Biotech]** **PDS Biotech receives $3.9 million from NantWorks warrant exercise** [X / Twitter (@BioStocks)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120140927939539008) — *X / Twitter (@BioStocks)*
  - PDS Biotech announced NantWorks exercised warrants at $0.22 per share, generating approximately $3.9 million in gross proceeds.

- **Billionaire Bill Ackman launches brain research institute** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/09/bill-ackman-launches-new-brain-research-institute/) — *STAT*
  - Investor Bill Ackman committed capital to establish a novel brain research institute to support early-stage translational neuroscience.

## Public Health & Policy

- **BIO outlines 'BIOAdvance' policy proposal to preserve U.S. biotech leadership** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/bio-bioadvance-proposal-us-trial-competition-china/874162/) — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Industry group BIO released a seven-point legislative initiative calling for federal measures to streamline U.S. clinical trial execution and strengthen domestic competitiveness against China's biopharma expansion.

- **Global analysis finds mixed progress on LMIC drug access by major pharma** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/10/access-to-key-drugs-mixed-in-poor-countries-cancer-diabetes/) — *STAT*
  - A comprehensive report assessing pharmaceutical access initiatives in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) concluded that rollout of essential oncology and diabetes drugs remains highly inconsistent across participating firms.

- **U.S. midterm elections open pathways for Medicaid expansion in three states** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/medicaid-expansion-holdout-states-midterm-election-power-shift/) — *STAT*
  - Midterm election outcomes in Texas, Georgia, and Wisconsin may enable state-level Medicaid expansion, potentially extending coverage to over one million uninsured individuals.

***

**Worth watching:** **[Big Pharma]** Bayer's commercial launch of Sunharbo (asundexian) will be a critical test of whether FXIa inhibition can overcome long-standing bleeding safety trade-offs in secondary stroke prevention.

- Biology & Health
    - [Frontier AI Labs Are the Real Competition](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zc_VhdgL93A) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Sergei Polevikov asserts that incumbent healthcare technology companies must begin viewing frontier AI labs as direct competitors.
        - The competitive threat and market disruption from frontier AI labs may not be immediate, but requires strategic positioning by traditional healthtech firms.
        - Digital health companies must reevaluate their competitive landscape beyond conventional industry rivals to account for advancing frontier AI capabilities.
    - [AI Could Cure Diseases and Become Incredibly Dangerous](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/hJmSiOskwks) -- Health2Tech
        - Alison Curfman highlights AI’s capacity to significantly accelerate medical innovation and potentially cure diseases.
        - Alongside its therapeutic promise, AI deployment introduces severe safety risks that healthcare organizations must actively manage.
        - Healthcare leaders are urged to address the dual nature of AI by balancing rapid technological advancement with strict risk mitigation.
